messages:
deploy-bot: Maintenance window scheduled: 2026-04-20 01:30-02:45 UTC. Scope: hosted inference (generation + embeddings) in eu-central-1 and us-west-2. Work: runtime image patch (v2.4.1), driver security fixes, and publish trimmed release notes. Rolling AZ drains; autoscaling paused for window.

Rhea (prodops): Need customer-facing artifacts: short statuspage blurb, an SMS for ops-critical customers, and an email for subscribers. Also want a one-line release-notes summary we can link from the status update.

Dmitri (eng-oncall): Impact summary: rolling drains cause transient 502/503 responses up to ~40s per instance. We'll run a 10% canary in eu-central-1 for 12m then continue if metrics stable. If canary shows >1.5% 5xx or p95 spike >250ms, pause and pin to v2.3.x. No schema or API changes.

Leah (support): I'll prepare CS templates: retry/backoff wording, guidance about idempotency for webhook consumers, and a short line to reassure Dedicated/private customers (they're unaffected unless on managed autoscale). Also prep an escalation stub for enterprise on-call contacts.

Anika (sre): Abort conditions: sustained 5xx >2% over 10m during ramp, p95 >350ms for 15m, or any kernel-level panic/oom on >1 node. On abort: halt rollout, switch canaries back to v2.3.x, open incident channel, and trigger oncall rotation. Post-change must pass smoke checks before autoscale resumes.

Rhea (prodops): Draft statuspage snippet (short):

Scheduled maintenance: Runtime patch for hosted API in eu-central-1 & us-west-2.
Start: 2026-04-20 01:30 UTC — End: 2026-04-20 02:45 UTC (approx).
Impact: Short rolling request failures (502/503) and possible transient latency increases.
Customer action: None. Dedicated/private deployments unaffected unless using managed autoscaler. Updates: status.redwood.ai

Rhea (prodops): Draft email subject/body:
Subject: Planned maintenance — brief interruption to hosted API (Apr 20)
Body: Hi — We will perform scheduled maintenance on April 20 affecting hosted API in EU-CENTRAL and US-WEST. You may see brief request failures or higher latency during the window. No action needed. We will post live updates to status.redwood.ai and contact enterprise customers directly if action is required.

Rhea (prodops): SMS (ops-critical):
"Planned maintenance Apr 20 01:30 UTC — brief hosted API interruptions possible in EU/US. status.redwood.ai"

Leah (support): CS FAQ snippets: What happened? Why did I see 503s? How to retry safely? When should I open a ticket? (include thresholds). I'll stage these in Zendesk and the support playbook.

Dmitri (eng-oncall): Canary metrics: 5xx rate, p50/p95 latency, token throughput, KV cache hit ratio, and tail latencies for long-context requests. Canary threshold: investigate >1.5% 5xx; abort >2.5% 5xx. Also watch memory and kernel logs for regressions.

Anika (sre): Post-maint smoke checklist (must be green before autoscale unpause):
1) Synthetic generation and embedding probes passing in both regions.
2) p50/p95 within 15% of baseline.
3) KV cache hit ratio within 5% of baseline.
4) No increase in kernel exceptions in last 30 minutes.
5) Error budget and SLOs reviewed; no sustained burn.

Leah (support): Will queue the statuspage update for T-60 and schedule the email for T-45. Also preparing a short "what changed" blurb for customers who notice perf differences after the maintenance.

Rhea (prodops): Good. Dmitri — please set the automation to pause at 10% for manual check, and again at 50%. Keep the rollback pin configured and make sure the diagnostics hooks (heap dumps, kernel logs) are enabled for the canary nodes.

Dmitri (eng-oncall): Will do. Canary starts in 20m. Rollout automation set to pause at 10% and 50% with 15m hold each. Notifying #eng-oncall and #support.

deploy-notify-bot: Canary will begin in 20 minutes. Publishing notices to oncall channels and to the maintenance draft on status.redwood.ai.

Rhea (prodops): Thanks team — leaving this thread open for any late changes. :white_check_mark:
